title: K8s node lifecycle incident - debugging notes (scratchpad)
content:
Summary:
- Random subset of new nodes in cluster fail to transition Ready after autoscaling / helm chart rollout (control-plane healthy).
- Symptoms: kubelet NotReady, containerd crashing on some hosts, recent cloud-init failures.
- Impact: ~3-5% of scaled nodes unusable, causes pod scheduling backlog and helm chart post-install hooks time out.

Timeline / notes (raw):
2026-02-20 09:10 - alert from monitoring: node-not-ready spike (3 nodes) in us-west1 cluster.
- Checked GCP console, instances show RUNNING.
- kubectl get nodes: 3 nodes show "NotReady" with taint node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoSchedule on older ones.

Commands run / outputs:
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
  NAME                                STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP    EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE             KERNEL-VERSION
  gke-cluster-default-pool-1-abcde    NotReady   <none>   12m   v1.28.4   10.0.1.12     34.68.120.10  Ubuntu 22.04.4 LTS    5.19.0-40-generic

- kubectl describe node gke-cluster-default-pool-1-abcde
  Conditions:
    Ready        False    KubeletNotReady  9m   kubelet has not synced: timed out waiting for the condition
  Events:
    Warning   KubeletNotReady   9m   kubelet, gke-cluster-default-pool-1-abcde   Kubelet has failed to start: exit code 1

- ssh to node and check systemd logs:
  sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | sed -n '1,120p'
  ERROR: failed to start kubelet: failed to create runtime: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start containerd: exit status 1

- sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200
  Feb 20 08:57:10 hostname containerd[1234]: panic: runtime inconsistency detected
  Feb 20 08:57:10 hostname containerd[1234]: goroutine 1 [running]:
  ...
  Feb 20 08:57:11 hostname containerd[1234]: failed to load snapshotter: corrupted metadata

Hypothesis 1: disk corruption on affected VMs or corrupted containerd state after image pre-pull.
- Checked /var/lib/containerd; snap meta DB shows odd size. Tried backup rename:
  sudo systemctl stop kubelet containerd
  sudo mv /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/containerd.broken-$(date +%s)
  sudo systemctl start containerd
  Result: containerd starts clean, kubelet moves to Ready after ~45s.
- But this loses local image cache; pods need image pull. For ephemeral scale-up this might be acceptable but not ideal.

Hypothesis 2: bootstrap provisioning (cloud-init/daemon) race causes containerd to start with partially written DB. Possibly caused by preemptible/spot recovery or disk snapshot restore.
- Checked cloud-init logs: /var/log/cloud-init.log shows repeated "WriteTimeoutError" when writing snapshot metadata during pre-pull step (custom image init).

Temporarily mitigations applied 2026-02-20 11:00:
- Added node-init post-start script to check containerd DB integrity before enabling kubelet:
  if [ -d /var/lib/containerd ] && [ -f /var/lib/containerd/initial_snapshot_meta ]; then
    check-tool --repair /var/lib/containerd || mv /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/containerd.broken-$(date +%s)
  fi
  systemctl restart containerd

- Effect: reduced NotReady spikes but still occasional failures.

Helm / Chart related notes:
- Problem observed during rolling deploy of ingress controller (chart v2.3.1) which triggers daemonset updates / pre-pull hooks.
- Some nodes were terminated and recreated by autoscaler while helm hooks were running -> pre-pull step attempted on new node concurrently. If node early-boot had interrupted write, containerd DB corrupted.

Repro attempt steps (local cluster):
1) start k8s node using cloud-init script that pre-pulls images and writes containerd snapshot metadata.
2) Simulate interruption: kill containerd during metadata write (kill -9)
3) reboot node and observe containerd failure to start with "corrupted metadata".

Repro results: consistent.

Next actions (todo list):
- [ ] Add pre-flight containerd integrity check to image used for nodes (image builder/packer) so new nodes boot with a clean /var/lib/containerd or safe-restore path.
- [ ] Update GCP instance template to include init script that moves broken DB and restarts containerd + kubelet if startup logs show corrupted metadata.
- [ ] Add kubelet readiness probe delay for first 2 minutes to avoid marking nodes NotReady too early when init tasks are running (but careful: can hide real Kubelet failures).
- [ ] Investigate whether autoscaler/helm rollout concurrency can be limited (use maxSurge: 1 or pause hooks).
- [ ] Add detection alert for repeated containerd panics in node logs (monitoring rule on containerd stderr).
- [ ] Run offline image pre-pull via DaemonSet after node joins instead of pre-pulling in cloud-init to reduce boot-time file corruption risk.

Useful commands/snippets (copied for reference):
- Check nodes not ready with reason:
  kubectl get nodes --no-headers | awk '{print $2, $1}' | grep NotReady
\- SSH automation to salvage node quickly:
  gcloud compute ssh $NODE --zone $ZONE --command "sudo systemctl stop kubelet containerd && sudo mv /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/containerd.broken-$(date +%s) && sudo systemctl start containerd kubelet"
\- containerd-check script (quick):
  #!/bin/bash
  set -e
  if [ -f /var/lib/containerd/metadata.db ]; then
    sqlite3 /var/lib/containerd/metadata.db 'pragma quick_check;' || exit 1
  fi
  exit 0

Notes / open questions:
- Why only a small subset of nodes? Theory: certain host images / zones have higher IO latency causing cloud-init writes to time out. Need correlation with zone and machine type.
- Are preemptible/spot nodes more affected? Check labels for spot instances.
- Is the containerd version we ship tolerant to interrupted writes? Consider upgrading or switching to a more robust snapshotter config.

Logs / snippets saved to GCS:
- gs://redwood-logs/node-corruption/2026-02-20/gke-cluster-default-pool-1-abcde-journal.log
- gs://redwood-logs/node-corruption/2026-02-20/containerd-metadata-dump.tar.gz

Reference runbook pointers:
- confluence:node-lifecycle-runbook (TODO add a 'containerd corruption' section)

If I/O latency is root cause then long-term fixes:
- Use local-ssd or tune cloud-init to use atomic tmpfs writes and fsync steps.
- Move pre-pull to after node Ready; use daemonset with init containers and back-off.
- Add a small startup service that validates container runtime metadata before systemd enables kubelet.

Scratchpad (commands to try next on one affected host):
- sudo systemctl stop kubelet containerd
- sudo mv /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/containerd.broken-$(date +%s)
- sudo systemctl start containerd
- sudo tail -n 200 /var/log/syslog | sed -n '1,200p'
- kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=$NODE -n kube-system --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 50

Random notes to self:
- Remember to coordinate with infra terraform changes: don't roll instance templates during a large helm rollout.
- Good quick mitigation: pipeline step to drain and recreate only limited subset when pre-pull hooks scheduled.

End of scratchpad.
